Not a game I'm ever going to "complete", not a game I'll ever have the confidence to play online, but my god, what a labour of love. I don't always love the track design - there's a few gimmicks here and there, especially with corners, that outright piss me off at times - and it does have an incredibly high skill ceiling that will take time to master if you really want to get the most out of it, but otherwise I don't know what else you could possibly want in a modern WipeOut clone. The weapons are useful without being game-breaking, there's an insane variety in ship and course types, the OST is just 100% bangers, the graphic design is on point, the race modes are great (I particularly love the Speed (1994)-esque survival mode, I'd love to see a whole game built around that gimmick), and even the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI feels well-balanced, a task many racing game devs still can't get right even with AAA publisher backing.

Holy Moly this game has completely taken me by storm! I am so thoroughly impressed with this game on every level. It flawlessly reproduces the Wipeout gameplay we love with amazing visuals and performance to accompany the air tight controls. The visuals aren't technically cutting edge mind you but are artistically beautiful and optimized to near perfection. That is not to say the game does not look visually stunning at times either though and if you play with all settings enable and no retro effects on you will get a striking game that holds up well at just about any resolution. 

That said the game is clearly aiming for a PS / PS2 style presentation with its tech and gives players an awesome assortment of effects to achieve just that. You can enable affine texture swim, dithering, and decreased draw distances to name a few, for a thoroughly 32 bit experience. or you can go for a cleaner higher resolution look. The visuals and assets are well suited to either in my opinion honestly. I personally have opted for a more PS2 + type look almost by playing at 1024x768 @85HZ on my CRT with only dithering enabled. The result is an absurdly smooth looking game with a very pleasing look. The game also offers a rather robust CRT filter with multiple levels to its various settings as well IN ADDITION to everything I've already discussed.

Just to touch on the gameplay one more time. As mentioned before, the game delivers a shockingly faithful Wipeout racing experience. The left and right air brake system, unique boost style gauge, and excellent sense of speed. I think it stands right alongside Wipeout Omega Collection as a phenomenal futuristic arcade racing experience.

Fantastic game, the visuals, the vibes, the music, OH MY GOD THE MUSIC are just top-notch. In my opinion the game is worth buying for the soundtrack alone, you won't find better techno/electronica in any modern game. Can't tell you the number of hours the soundtrack was just playing in the background when I was doing other things/playing other games.

If you're a fan of classic Wipeout games, or the PS1/5th Gen era in general, this game is must have, especially considering how damn cheap it is even with all the DLCs. And the DLCs are well worth it, they add amazing tracks and ships.

The game's modding support is also amazing, be it via Steam Workshop or any other means, you can add whatever you want, hell, you can fully recreate any of the three original Wipeout games in Ballistic NG, down to the UI/HUD.

If I was to cite a single most prominent problem this game has - it's the difficulty of the higher speed classes. I can tell this game was made BY hardcore Wipeout players FOR hardcore Wipeout players. And while they can finally find the challenge they seek in this game, everyone else is out of luck. I was able to finish most of the Wipeout games and somewhat comfortably play on higher speed classes, but not in this game. Seriously, just search a video of some pro player running on the highest speed - the ship barely follows the course, usually it flies well above it ignoring most of the turns and obstacles. It looks janky as hell and, frankly speaking, plain unenjoyable.

I was able to convince a couple of friends to buy the game and play it with me, and we just stick to the lower speed classes because the game becomes nearly unplayable around Zen.

Overall, I highly recommend buying it, just know what to expect - it's a VERY hard game that looks and sounds amazing, especially if you're into retro/vintage gaming. Very fun with friends, too. If you're fine with never finishing the game and sticking to the lower speed classes, it's an amazing experience.

BallisticNG, developed and published by Neognosis, is a high-speed anti-gravity racing game that proudly wears its retro inspirations on its sleeve while carving out a deeply polished identity of its own. Designed as a spiritual successor to the classic hovercraft racers of the late 1990s, it captures the essence of that era’s breakneck pacing and technical control while layering in modern customization, modding support, and mechanical refinement. From the moment you launch into your first race, it becomes clear that BallisticNG is less about casual arcade thrills and more about mastery, precision, and the pure exhilaration of speed.

At its core, BallisticNG is built around anti-gravity craft that glide inches above the track surface. Unlike traditional racing games where tire grip defines control, here momentum and airbrake management are everything. The ships feel weighty yet responsive, and maintaining optimal racing lines requires careful balancing of thrust and braking inputs. Learning to use the airbrakes effectively is essential, especially on tighter circuits with sharp chicanes and sudden elevation shifts. Early races can feel punishing, but as familiarity with the physics grows, so does the satisfaction of cleanly navigating a complex corner at full speed.

The tracks themselves are varied and thoughtfully designed. Neon-lit cityscapes, industrial complexes, and sprawling futuristic environments provide distinct atmospheres while demanding different racing strategies. Some tracks reward technical finesse with tight, winding layouts, while others emphasize raw acceleration on extended straightaways. Verticality and environmental hazards add further complexity, forcing players to adapt rather than rely on repetition. Each circuit encourages memorization and refinement, rewarding those willing to invest time into perfecting their lap times.

A significant strength of BallisticNG lies in its extensive single-player content. The campaign spans multiple speed classes, each escalating in intensity and demanding sharper reflexes. Events include traditional races alongside time trials, eliminator modes, and survival-style challenges. This variety keeps progression engaging and ensures that players are consistently tested in different ways. Higher speed classes in particular transform the experience into a near-sensory overload, where even minor mistakes can cost a podium finish.

Customization and mod support elevate the game beyond its base content. Players can create and import custom tracks, ships, campaigns, and even music, turning BallisticNG into a flexible racing platform rather than a static release. This robust toolkit has fostered a dedicated community that continues to expand the game’s offerings. For players who enjoy tinkering or experimenting with new content, this openness significantly extends replay value.

Visually, the game deliberately channels a retro aesthetic reminiscent of early 3D console racers, but it does so with modern clarity and smooth performance. The stylized low-poly environments and vibrant color palettes evoke nostalgia without feeling outdated. Frame rates remain stable even at extreme speeds, which is critical for a game where reaction time determines success. The inclusion of cockpit view and VR support further enhances immersion for those seeking an even more intense racing experience.

The soundtrack complements the gameplay perfectly. Electronic tracks with driving rhythms amplify the sense of momentum and immersion. Combined with the rising pitch of engines and the rush of environmental sound effects, the audio design reinforces the adrenaline-fueled atmosphere. Long stretches of focused racing often create a flow state where visuals, sound, and input blend seamlessly.

Multiplayer options add competitive longevity. Local split-screen allows for shared couch competition, while online functionality supports racing against others. Though the active player base can fluctuate, the infrastructure supports custom content and varied race settings, making organized matches particularly engaging.

BallisticNG does not cater to players seeking immediate accessibility. Its learning curve can be steep, particularly for those unfamiliar with anti-gravity racing mechanics. However, that difficulty becomes part of its appeal. Every improvement in lap time feels earned, and mastering a demanding track at high speeds delivers a uniquely rewarding sense of accomplishment.

Ultimately, BallisticNG stands as both a tribute to classic anti-gravity racers and a fully realized modern interpretation of the genre. Its combination of technical depth, customization freedom, and high-speed intensity makes it a standout indie racing experience. For players who appreciate precision-based gameplay and are willing to invest time into mastering its mechanics, it offers one of the most exhilarating and satisfying racing experiences available on Steam.
